title: Fractional coordinates produce an integral point outside a proper column sublattice
statement: Let $r\geq1$ and let $A$ be an $r\times r$ integer matrix with $\det A\ne0$ [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Regard its columns $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ as elements of $\mathbf Z^r\subset\mathbf Q^r$. These columns are linearly independent over $\mathbf Q$. For every $y\in\mathbf Z^r$ outside their integer span $\{\sum_i m_i v_i:m_i\in\mathbf Z\}$, there exists a unique $b\in\mathbf Q^r$ with $Ab=y$. Define $z_i=\lfloor b_i\rfloor\in\mathbf Z$, where $z_i\leq b_i<z_i+1$, put $a_i=b_i-z_i$, and put $x=y-Az\in\mathbf Z^r$. Then $x=Aa\ne0$, $0\leq a_i<1$ for every $i$, and there is $j$ with $0<a_j<1$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Tag 07DQ (algebra-lemma-matrix-left-inverse, algebra.tex lines 2688--2691), adjugate identity. The rational-coordinate floor construction is an agent-supplied refinement, not a verbatim Stacks assertion. Extracts old proof step 5 of lem-trf-fs-chart-free-factorization.

proof.text: Let M be the entrywise image of A in the rationals. RingHom.map_det identifies det M with the integer cast of det A, so det M is nonzero. Put C = (det M)⁻¹ • adjugate M. Apply both identities in [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity] over the commutative ring ℚ. Distributing scalar multiplication and cancelling the nonzero determinant gives CM = MC = 1.

source.place: Tag 07DQ (algebra-lemma-matrix-left-inverse), proof, adjugate identity at lines 2688--2691; rational-coordinate argument supplied by NM.

proof.text: Mathlib Matrix.linearIndependent_cols_of_det_ne_zero applied to M gives rational independence of the columns. Multiplying M u = M v by C and using CM = 1 proves injectivity of M.mulVec. For the given integer vector y, define b = C y over ℚ. Then M b = MC y = y. If M b′ = y, injectivity applied to M b′ = M b gives b′ = b.

source.place: Tag 07DQ (algebra-lemma-matrix-left-inverse), proof, adjugate identity at lines 2688--2691; rational-coordinate argument supplied by NM.

proof.text: For every i use Int.floor_le and Int.lt_floor_add_one to obtain floor(b i) ≤ b i < floor(b i) + 1. Subtract floor(b i), using sub_nonneg and sub_lt_iff_lt_add′, to obtain 0 ≤ b i - floor(b i) < 1. These floor inequalities apply equally to negative rational coordinates.

source.place: Tag 07DQ (algebra-lemma-matrix-left-inverse), proof, adjugate identity at lines 2688--2691; rational-coordinate argument supplied by NM.

proof.text: For any integer vector z, RingHom.map_mulVec says that the rational image of A z is M applied to the rational image of z. Set z i = floor(b i). Using this identity, M.mulVec_sub, and M b = y, identify the rational image of x = y - A z with M(b - z). If x = 0 then A z = y, contradicting the outside-span hypothesis. If b - z were zero, the displayed identity and injectivity of the integer cast would force x = 0. Thus one coordinate b j - z j is nonzero. Its nonnegativity makes it strictly positive, and the upper bound from the preceding step is less than one.
